newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 8.76 pct in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 8.76 pct in profit-taking.

text.p: Turkish shares fell sharply on Tuesday amid heavy profit-taking which brokers said was an overdue correction to the recent strong rally.
The IMKB National-100 ended at 1,551, down 149 points, or 8.76 percent from Monday's all-time high close of 1,700. Its dollar value was 1.34 cents, down from Monday's 1.47-cent record.
Trade volume hit a new record for the fourth day in a row. It stood at 71.85 trillion lira ($619.4 million) against Monday's 69.48 trillion ($602.3 million).
"Today's fall was an expected development. The index's 1,500 level is seen as a new support level," said Deniz Ata from Alfa securities. The index brushed a low of 1,539 in the day.

Brokers said a privatisation board (OIB) announcement that only two bids were received in the sell-off tender of largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli also fuelled afternoon selling in Eregli which closed down 3,250 lira at 22,000.
The OIB said bids were made by two domestic investors for a 30-40 percent block stake offer in the Eregli tender which closed on Monday.
The index had surged 74.2 percent, breaking 17 record closes from January 2 to Monday's close. In dollar terms, it had jumped 61.5 percent in the same period.
The uptrend was further boosted by last Thursday's contitutional court ruling giving green light to Turk Telekom's sell-off. The index had soared 36 percent in the last three days.
